@DrNealDunnFL2 If my family isn’t compensated for my organs or no guarantee they go to 1981 and younger individuals, then I’ll be taking them with me to the crematorium. Anybody older than a millennial can kiss my ass. Y’all are what got us to this point.

At least 28 patients may not have been deceased during organ procurement, yet the admin's "reforms" are a masterclass in contradiction. The outrage is performative when the rot is systemic and the oversight is hollow.

While 17 Americans die daily awaiting transplant, the admin's Feb. 14 layoffs gutted modernization teams. CMS still uses 2022 data for oversight, and misaligned policies led to 9,275 kidneys being discarded in 2024 alone—an 83% increase. This isn't reform; it's managed decay.

Questioning officials is theater. The real question is why the admin is dismantling the cure while decrying the disease.

The OPTN Fee Collection Authority Act (S.532) is a critical step toward accountability, mandating GAO review of organ procurement fees and practices. HHS investigations found 28 cases where patients showed signs of life during procurement attempts—a systemic failure exposing lax oversight.

While the bill’s transparency measures (Section 2(d)(4)) force OPOs to disclose fee usage, Network for Hope’s merger with Kentucky Organ Donor Affiliates didn’t purge the rot: former officials linked to these “disturbing” practices remain entrenched. RFK Jr.’s reforms demand decertification for protocol violations, but the 3-year sunset clause on fee authority risks reverting to status quo.

Real accountability requires dismantling OPO monopolies, not just shuffling bureaucrats.

The entrenched power structures and recurring protocol breaches demand more than temporary fixes—see the documented evidence: https://t.co/uJeRVdvTga
@DrNealDunnFL2 @HouseCommerce Why aren't you mentioning the DOCTORS that are performing the theft of organs?

March 2025 HRSA findings showed patients alive during organ procurement. Trump admin sat silent as 8,400 died waiting—then staged "sweeping reforms" days before today's hearing. Their theater: blaming Biden's committees while extending CMS's failed metrics that'll decertify half of OPOs by 2026.  

CMS's 2024-25 reports use junk data even the AOPO calls "misaligned." Result? 28% of kidneys wasted in 2023, 25% in 2024. Every unused organ represents 26 million allocation offers gone unanswered. Yet the admin peddles horror stories about individual cases while preserving systems that discard 1 in 4 kidneys.  

Accountability delayed is patients denied. Your oversight enables their negligence.

The real threat to public trust isn’t oversight—it’s OPOs cutting corners and failing patients. The HHS investigation under Secretary Kennedy exposed systemic negligence, including cases where organ procurement began on patients showing signs of life. The OPTN Fee Collection Authority Act (S.532) tried to inject transparency with mandatory reporting, but the system’s rot runs deeper.

Taxpayers fund these organizations to save lives, not to prioritize bureaucratic self-preservation. When OPOs misclassify causes of death, ignore consent protocols, and rush procurement, they betray both donors and recipients.

Oversight isn’t the problem—it’s the only path to accountability.

The Sickle Cell Disease Comprehensive Care Act sounds compassionate—until you realize Medicaid already hemorrhages $55B annually in improper payments while bureaucrats ignore eligibility audits. Coordinated care? Great. But funneling more cash into a broken system without fixing systemic fraud is like slapping a Band-Aid on a bullet wound.

Where’s the accountability for ER misuse by non-citizens or duplicate programs draining resources? Real reform starts with auditing every dollar before expanding benefits.

Until then, it’s just another bureaucratic shell game—patients lose, taxpayers lose, and the cycle continues.

The real numbers behind Medicaid’s waste and the unanswered questions on oversight are all here: https://t.co/0bDmKpCDLu
